paper_identity.title: Inhibition of ETS1/DRP1 axis attenuates intervertebral disc degeneration by suppressing excessive mitochondrial fission.

genes.direction: upregulated in severe human IVDD and NPC senescence

mechanism.evidence: ETS1 was upregulated in severe human IVDD and correlated with disc degeneration severity and NPC senescence. Mechanistically, inflammatory cytokines induced ETS1 upregulation, which directly bound to the dynamin 1-like (DNM1L, encoding DRP1) promoter and activated its transcription.
Increased DRP1 triggered excessive mitochondrial fission, leading to reactive oxygen species accumulation
excessive mitochondrial fission, leading to reactive oxygen species accumulation, NPC senescence, and ECM catabolism

findings.evidence: Inhibition of ETS1 via AAV5-mediated RNA interference or targeting DRP1 with CRISPR/dCas9-KRAB system or Mdivi-1 alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, ECM degradation, and attenuated IVDD progression

why_this_paper_matters: This paper identifies a novel pathogenic mechanism (ETS1/DRP1 axis) in intervertebral disc degeneration, providing potential therapeutic targets for IVDD. The findings demonstrate how inflammatory cytokines drive NPC senescence through ETS1-mediated DRP1 activation, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and ECM degradation. This mechanism offers a new approach for treating IVDD by targeting the ETS1/DRP1 axis.
